newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Launch of Citizens First campaign.
newsitem.headline: Launch of Citizens First campaign.

text.p: The European Union will launch an information campaign on Tuesday to make the single market more comprehensible and user-friendly for its 370 million citizens.

On the sidelines of the Internal Market Council a special ceremony will be held at the European Parliament at 1300 (1200 GMT) involving Commission President Jacques Santer, single market commissioner Mario Monti, and a host of ministers and parliamentarians to launch the "citizens first" campaign

The open market where goods, people, services and capital should have been able to move freely from January 1, 1993, has often been criticised for being business-oriented and for ignoring the ordinary man and woman on the street.
But the European Commission has argued that ordinary citizens do not make use of it because they do not know what it can do for them because it has been badly explained.
The campaign will operate through brochures, television spots, phone lines and a web site on the Internet.

It will try to explain to people exactly how they can live, work and study in other parts of the Union, how they can benefit from EU rules on equal opportunities and how they can claim compensation for faulty goods bought in another country.
